data.cultural_impact: In Islamic culture, Kohl has been extensively used since ancient times for cosmetic purposes, predominantly for eyeliner. With its origins predating Islam, it has been an essential part of various traditions. It has symbolic meanings in many cultures of the Middle East and beyond. For instance, Kohl was used by various nomadic populations of the Arabian Peninsula to protect their eyes from desert dust and direct sunlight. In the modern context, its usage is widespread in the Middle East and among the Muslim diaspora worldwide as a traditional cosmetic.
data.spiritual_significance: In various Islamic traditions, Kohl is believed to have spiritual significance. It is regarded as a Sunnah (practice following the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)). Furthermore, it is believed that Kohl acts as a shield against the evil eye and protects the eyes from harm. Some scholars suggest that the belief may have originated from the Quranic verse, "And We made the vision which We gave to Moses and his brother (Aaron) a trial for Pharaoh and his people; it was a manifest trial. So when they saw it, they were awe-struck by it; and let loose (sheep) (for them) in the land. They said: "This is indeed a marvelous magic!" (Quran 7:107). Therefore, using Kohl is often said to help uphold one's faith and provide protection both in this life and the next.
